The patient presents with a constellation of systemic symptoms — fatigue, cognitive dysfunction (“trouble concentrating”), exertional dyspnea, dizziness, and *paradoxical cold-relieved finger pain* — all evolving over ~3 weeks. Notably absent are classic features of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (no rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, alopecia, joint swelling/stiffness, fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, or neurologic symptoms like numbness/weakness). The paradoxical improvement of finger pain with cold is unusual but may reflect microvascular phenomena related to extreme thrombocytosis (e.g., transient platelet-mediated microthrombi causing ischemic discomfort that resolves with vasoconstriction or reduced platelet activation in cold).
